idiom_name: buffered channel make(chan T, N) with close() and range (or select with done/context)
implementation_notes: The channel type is the pattern: ch := make(chan T, N) gives the bounded buffer, a send blocks while the buffer is full, a receive blocks while it is empty, and close(ch) after the last send terminates the consumer's for v := range ch loop - the sending side is the producer, the receiving side the consumer, and no mutex, condition variable or queue is written by hand. Fan-out (several goroutines receiving from one channel) and fan-in (a merge goroutine multiplexing channels) follow directly, and select with a done channel or ctx.Done() adds cancellation to a blocked send or receive. Use an unbuffered channel (make(chan T)) when every item must be handed off synchronously, and buffer a known number of values when a stage must not block immediately.
pitfalls: Sending on a closed channel panics and closing twice panics: exactly one owner closes, exactly once, after the last send.
If a downstream stage stops early, blocked senders leak goroutines forever; give producers a done channel or context and select on it.
An unbuffered channel is a rendezvous - the producer waits for a receiver on every item, which serializes the two sides rather than decoupling them.
Buffer capacity is fixed at make() time; a queue whose depth must grow needs a different structure.
